Voici le rapport d'audit du subagent `ux-designer`, transmis verbatim : ## Audit Report — `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/design_target.html` ### Summary Accessibility and usability audit of a 4-field account-settings form fragment (email input, inline validation message, a "Save changes" control, and an icon-only dismiss/clear button) against WCAG 2.2 AA and Nielsen's 10 heuristics. File was not edited; findings below are audit-only. ### User and task - **User segment:** returning account holder correcting a rejected email address; includes keyboard-only users and screen-reader users. - **Task:** correct the invalid email field and save the change. - **Success criterion:** field error is understood without sight of color alone, form is submittable and dismissible entirely via keyboard/AT, no accidental submission. - **Failure modes:** error not perceivable/associated to AT users, save action unreachable by keyboard, unlabeled control triggers unintended submission. ### Stakes classification **High** — accessibility-critical form with error handling (account settings + validation state), per Move 2 criteria. --- ## Violations | # | Element (locatable excerpt) | Criterion violated | Severity | Minimal fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `` (line 13) | **WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A)** — placeholder is the only label; it disappears once the user types and is not exposed as a label by the accessibility tree. | Serious | Add `` and `id="email"` on the input; placeholder may remain as a supplementary hint, not the label. | | 2 | Same `` (line 13) | **WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA)** — a field collecting a common user-identity data type (email) has no `autocomplete` token. | Moderate | Add `autocomplete="email"`. | | 3 | `Invalid format` (line 17) | **WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA)** — computed contrast of `#FF0000` on the default white body background is **~4.0:1**, below the 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text. (Not a 1.4.1 "use of color" violation — the text itself already conveys the meaning, so 1.4.1 does not strictly apply; the fixture's own inline comment mislabels the defect. The real, checkable defect is contrast.) | Serious | Darken to a red with ≥4.5:1 against white (e.g. `#B00000`), or increase weight/size to qualify for the 3:1 large-text threshold and re-verify. | | 4 | Same `` (line 17) | **WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification (A)** — the error text is not programmatically associated with the field it describes (no `aria-describedby` linking `input#email` to the span). | Serious | Give the span an `id` and add `aria-describedby=""` on the input; also set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input while the error is present. | | 5 | Same `` (line 17) | **WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)** — if this message appears dynamically after validation, it is not exposed as a status message, so a screen-reader user not focused on the field will never hear it. | Moderate | Wrap the message container in `role="alert"` (or `aria-live="assertive"`) so it is announced without requiring focus to move. | | 6 | `
